🎬 Just Mercy (2019)

Just Mercy follows Bryan Stevenson, a young Harvard-educated lawyer who moves to Alabama in the late 1980s to defend people who have been unfairly treated by the criminal justice system. Determined to provide legal representation to those who cannot afford it, Bryan establishes an organization dedicated to helping prisoners facing wrongful convictions and harsh sentences. One of his most challenging cases involves Walter McMillian, a man sentenced to death for a murder he insists he did not commit. Despite serious problems with the evidence and testimony used to convict Walter, Bryan encounters resistance from local authorities and a legal system unwilling to acknowledge its mistakes. As he investigates the case, he uncovers troubling inconsistencies, racial prejudice, and powerful obstacles that threaten his efforts to secure justice. Alongside his colleague Eva Ansley, Bryan works tirelessly to expose the truth while developing meaningful relationships with prisoners and their families. From emotional courtroom battles and shocking revelations to personal sacrifices and moments of extraordinary courage, his journey demonstrates the importance of compassion and perseverance. Based on a true story, the film combines powerful performances, emotional storytelling, and gripping legal drama while exploring justice, racial inequality, wrongful convictions, human dignity, and the belief that everyone deserves a fair chance.

🎭 Genre: Biography • Drama • Legal Drama

⭐ IMDb: 7.6/10

⏱️ Runtime: 2h 17m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Destin Daniel Cretton
